1 # Releasing Hey Reachy 2 3 Signed artifacts are produced locally; CI only publishes the GitHub release with 4 generated notes. Credentials never enter the repository or CI. 5 6 ## One-time setup 7 8 1. **App Store Connect API key** — App Store Connect → Users and Access → 9 Integrations → App Store Connect API → Team Keys, role **App Manager**. 10 Download the `.p8` once and write the credentials file: 11 12 ```bash 13 mkdir -p ~/.config/reachy-mini 14 cat > ~/.config/reachy-mini/release.env <<'CONF' 15 REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX 16 REACHY_ASC_KEY_ID=XXXXXXXXXX 17 REACHY_ASC_ISSUER_ID=xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx 18 REACHY_ASC_KEY_PATH=/Users/you/.config/reachy-mini/AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8 19 CONF 20 ``` 21 22 2. **App IDs and the App Group** — the first signed build with 23 `-allowProvisioningUpdates` registers the bundle ids 24 (`com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`, `.Widget`), but the 25 `group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini` capability must be added by hand in 26 Xcode's Signing & Capabilities, once per App ID (app and widget separately, 27 iOS and macOS separately). `xcodebuild` cannot create it. 28 29 3. **App Store Connect app record** — My Apps → New App: 30 - Name: **Hey Reachy**; if taken, fall back to “Hey Reachy — robot remote”. 31 - Subtitle: **Control your Reachy Mini**. 32 - Bundle id `com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`. 33 - The description must state it is an unofficial client for Reachy Mini by 34 Pollen Robotics. A public TestFlight link goes through Beta App Review, so 35 the name is checked before any App Store submission. 36 - App Privacy: no data collected. The app talks to the robot on the local 37 network and to Hugging Face with the user's own OAuth session; nothing is 38 sent to the developer. 39 - Encryption: answered in the Info.plist (`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption`), 40 ASC asks nothing per build. 41 42 4. **Developer ID Application certificate** (macOS) — Xcode → Settings → 43 Accounts → Manage Certificates → “+” → Developer ID Application. 44 45 5. **macOS ships through both channels**, so the Mac App Store one needs its own 46 signing assets besides the Developer ID certificate: Apple Distribution and 47 Mac Installer Distribution. `-allowProvisioningUpdates` creates them through 48 the Xcode account the same way it does for iOS. The app record already 49 carries a macOS platform beside the iOS one — `mise run asc -- versions list 50 --app 6799644194` shows both — so nothing has to be created in App Store 51 Connect. What is not automatic is the App Group: step 2 registers it per App 52 ID, and the macOS App ID is a separate one from the iOS App ID. 53 54 ## Each release 55 56 1. Bump `MARKETING_VERSION` in `Apps/Project.swift` (bare semver, e.g. `0.2.0`) 57 and land it on `main`. Build numbers are the commit count — nothing to bump. 58 2. Tag and push; the tag triggers the GitHub release with git-cliff notes: 59 60 ```bash 61 git tag 0.2.0 && git push origin 0.2.0 62 ``` 63 64 3. Produce and ship the artifacts: 65 66 ```bash 67 mise run release:ios # archive → TestFlight 68 mise run release:macos # archive → both macOS channels (see below) 69 gh release upload 0.2.0 Apps/DerivedData/Export/macOS/HeyReachy-0.2.0.zip 70 ``` 71 72 `release:macos` archives once and exports that archive twice, because 73 `-exportArchive` re-signs per method — the two artifacts are the same build: 74 75 | Channel | Method | Artifact | Ends up in | 76 | -------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------- | 77 | `developer-id` | notarize → staple | `Export/macOS/HeyReachy-.zip` | GitHub release, by hand | 78 | `appstore` | upload | `.pkg` (not kept) | TestFlight for macOS | 79 80 Developer ID runs first on purpose: it is the artifact that always ships, and a 81 failed App Store upload should not also cost you the zip. Pick one channel with 82 `--channel appstore` or `--channel developer-id`. 83 84 Both archive commands compile with the Xcode compilation cache off 85 (`COMPILATION_CACHE_ENABLE_CACHING=NO`) and then run 86 `Scripts/check-appintents-metadata.sh` against the archive before anything is 87 exported or uploaded. The intents live in a static SPM library, so the 88 Shortcuts app only ever sees what `appintentsmetadataprocessor` extracted into 89 `Metadata.appintents` — and extraction failing is a warning, never a build 90 error. TestFlight 0.1.1 shipped exactly that way: green archive, no actions in 91 the Shortcuts app. The check names every missing action instead; if it fails, 92 the fix is in the build, not in App Store Connect. 93 94 Dry runs: `mise run release:ios -- --no-upload` exports an `.ipa` without 95 uploading; `mise run release:macos -- --no-notarize` stops the Developer ID 96 channel after the signed export, and `--no-upload` makes the App Store channel 97 leave a `.pkg` in `Export/macOS/AppStore` instead of uploading it. Each flag 98 belongs to one channel and is ignored by the other. 99 100 ### When `-exportArchive` fails 101 102 Two failures land on the same step and have nothing to do with each other. 103 104 `productbuild failed` with `CSSMERR_CSP_USER_CANCELED` in the distribution log is 105 the keychain: the Mac Installer identity lives in `reachy-signing.keychain-db`, 106 and macOS put up an access dialog that a non-interactive run cannot answer — it 107 "cancels" itself after a few minutes. Authorize the key once and the keychain 108 keeps it: 109 110 ```bash 111 KC=~/Library/Keychains/reachy-signing.keychain-db 112 PW="$(cat ~/.config/reachy-mini/signing/keychain.pw)" 113 security unlock-keychain -p "$PW" "$KC" 114 security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k "$PW" "$KC" 115 ``` 116 117 `Failed to Use Accounts` is the Xcode account instead, and only the upload leg 118 needs one. Export locally and hand the artifact to the API key, which does the 119 upload, the group and the Beta App Review submission in one call: 120 121 ```bash 122 mise run asc -- publish testflight --app 6799644194 --platform IOS \ 123 --ipa "Apps/DerivedData/Export/iOS/Hey Reachy.ipa" \ 124 --group c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e \ 125 --wait --test-notes "…" --locale en-US --submit --confirm 126 ``` 127 128 A macOS `.pkg` is not a zip, so `asc` cannot read the version out of it: that one 129 also needs `--version` and `--build-number` (the commit count) spelled out. 130 131 ## The store listing 132 133 The App Store copy lives in this repository, at `metadata/` — `app-info/en-US.json` 134 for the fields that belong to the app (name, subtitle, privacy policy URL) and 135 `version//en-US.json` for the ones that belong to a version (description, 136 keywords, promotional text, support and marketing URLs). Edit those, then: 137 138 ```bash 139 mise run asc -- metadata validate --dir ./metadata 140 mise run asc -- metadata push --app 6799644194 --version 0.2.0 --platform IOS --dir ./metadata --dry-run 141 mise run asc -- metadata push --app 6799644194 --version 0.2.0 --platform IOS --dir ./metadata 142 ``` 143 144 Push once per platform — `IOS` and `MAC_OS` carry separate version localizations 145 off the same files. A version sitting in `WAITING_FOR_REVIEW` still takes the URL 146 fields (measured on 0.2.1), so a listing does not have to be pulled out of review 147 to repoint it. `whatsNew` is deliberately absent: Apple refuses it on an 148 app's **first** App Store version (`Attribute 'whatsNew' cannot be edited at this 149 time`), so release notes start with the second one. 150 151 Everything that is not a localization is set once and stays: category, content 152 rights, age rating, availability, price, and the reviewer contact and notes. They 153 are listed by `asc validate --app 6799644194 --version-id --platform

`, 154 which is the one command worth running before every submission — it prints an 155 ordered remediation plan and exits non-zero while anything is missing. 156 157 **It does not catch what rejected the macOS build.** An automated App Review check 158 reads the entitlements and refused 0.2.1 for carrying 159 `com.apple.security.network.server` "without matching functionality", while 160 `asc validate` reported zero blocking issues. The entitlement is required — WebRTC's 161 ICE binds UDP sockets and receives datagrams from a peer it never `connect()`ed to, 162 which App Sandbox counts as listening (`.claude/rules/networking.md`) — so the answer 163 is Apple's second option: keep it and justify it in **App Review Information**, which 164 is a per-version, per-platform record with a 4000-character limit and no presence in 165 `metadata/`. It lives only on the server, so a new version needs it written again, 166 and the check fires on every macOS submission that carries the key: 167 168 ```bash 169 mise run asc -- review details-for-version --version-id 170 mise run asc -- review details-update --id --notes "..." 171 ``` 172 173 Not to be confused with `testflight review edit`: Beta App Review and App Review keep 174 separate notes, and neither one is read by the other. A rejection's own text is in 175 Resolution Center, which the public API does not expose at all — `asc web review show` 176 reaches it, at the price of an Apple ID web session with 2FA. 177 178 Two of those answers are judgement calls, and both were decided against the two 179 Reachy apps already on the store rather than from first principles. Pollen's own 180 `Reachy Mini` (id 6766823749) sells the same community app catalogue this one 181 does — "browse and launch community apps instantly" — and stands at **9+** with 182 _Infrequent/Mild Cartoon or Fantasy Violence_ and _Mature/Suggestive Themes_, 183 which is a statement about what a community app might do rather than about the 184 app's own content. The independent `Reachy's Brain` (id 6757115923) is **4+** 185 with no advisories, but it ships no catalogue at all, so it is not the precedent 186 to copy. Hence: `USES_THIRD_PARTY_CONTENT`, because the Apps tab renders a Hugging 187 Face catalogue this project does not own, and every age-rating answer left at 188 `NONE` with an explicit `--age-rating-override-v2 NINE_PLUS` on top — declaring a 189 shelf position rather than asserting content the app does not contain. Both are 190 one `asc` command to revert. Their public halves are readable without a session: 191 `curl -s "https://itunes.apple.com/lookup?id="` carries 192 `contentAdvisoryRating`, `advisories` and `genres`; the content-rights 193 declaration is private and cannot be checked this way. 194 195 ## The public beta 196 197 `https://testflight.apple.com/join/CGjefT9a` — the **Public Beta** group, 198 `c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e`, capped at 500 testers. The link is in 199 the README; raising the cap is one `groups edit --public-link-limit`, lowering 200 it below the people who already joined is not. 201 202 Uploading is not distributing. An upload reaches the internal group by itself, 203 because `Internal` carries `hasAccessToAllBuilds`; the public group has to be 204 attached per build, per platform, and each one is its own Beta App Review: 205 206 ```bash 207 mise run asc -- builds add-groups --app 6799644194 --latest --platform IOS \ 208 --group c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e --submit --confirm 209 mise run asc -- builds add-groups --app 6799644194 --latest --platform MAC_OS \ 210 --group c48f6abb-c178-40a2-8747-b6513add766e --submit --confirm 211 mise run asc -- testflight review submissions list --build-id "" 212 ``` 213 214 What review reads lives at the app level, not the build level, so it is written 215 once and stays: the tester-facing text in `testflight app-localizations` 216 (description, feedback email, marketing URL, and the privacy policy — which has 217 to resolve, or review fails on a 404, so **enable Pages and open the URLs 218 first**), and the reviewer-facing contact and notes in `testflight review edit`. 219 220 **`metadata push` never reaches those.** `betaAppLocalizations` holds its own 221 copy of the marketing and privacy URLs, outside `metadata/` and outside every 222 version, so a store listing moved to a new host leaves TestFlight on the old one 223 until this runs too: 224 225 ```bash 226 mise run asc -- testflight app-localizations list --app 6799644194 227 mise run asc -- testflight app-localizations update --id "" \ 228 --marketing-url "https://alexey1312.github.io/reachy-mini-swift/" \ 229 --privacy-policy-url "https://alexey1312.github.io/reachy-mini-swift/privacy.html" 230 ``` 231 232 The reviewer notes carry the thing no reviewer can guess — that the app needs a robot nobody at 233 Apple has, that the Bluetooth sheet auto-presenting on first launch hides the 234 Local Network alert underneath it, and that Hugging Face sign-in is the one path 235 that completes without hardware. Beta App Review has no demo account to give, 236 because the app has no accounts. 237 238 Testers see the same What to Test note per build: 239 240 ```bash 241 mise run asc -- builds test-notes create --build-id "" \ 242 --locale en-US --whats-new "..." 243 ``` 244 245 ## Querying App Store Connect 246 247 `mise run asc` is the App Store Connect CLI with the same key already loaded — 248 `Scripts/asc.sh` maps the `REACHY_ASC_*` values onto the `ASC_*` names the tool 249 reads, so nothing is stored twice and no keychain profile exists to drift. 250 Everything after `--` goes to `asc`: 251 252 ```bash 253 mise run asc -- apps list 254 mise run asc -- builds list --app 6799644194 # did the TestFlight upload land? 255 mise run asc -- testflight beta-groups list --app 6799644194 256 ``` 257 258 `asc` resolves a stored profile before the environment, so an `asc auth login` 259 run by hand silently outranks this wrapper — `mise run asc -- auth status` 260 prints which of the two is answering. The key is App Manager, not Admin, so the 261 same limit release-ios.sh documents applies: it can read and submit, and it 262 cannot manage provisioning profiles. 263 264 The CLI also ships 23 agent skills (`asc install-skills`, pinned to a reviewed 265 commit) covering TestFlight, metadata, submissions and signing. 266 267 ## Xcode Cloud (optional, continuous TestFlight) 268 269 `Apps/ci_scripts/ci_post_clone.sh` makes a generated project buildable on 270 Xcode Cloud: it installs the pinned tools through the committed `bin/mise` 271 bootstrap, generates the workspace, and stamps `CI_BUILD_NUMBER` in as the 272 build number. Signing there is managed by Apple — no certificates leave the 273 account — and TestFlight distribution is a post-action checkbox. The setup 274 quirks (create the workflow from a local Xcode, start the build counter above 275 the last local upload, Git LFS is unsupported so never build the snapshot 276 scheme there) are commented at the top of the script. 277

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Archive the iOS app (Release, signed) and upload it to TestFlight.
3	#
4	#   mise run release:ios              # archive → upload to App Store Connect
5	#   mise run release:ios -- --no-upload   # archive → export an .ipa locally
6	#
7	# Signing and uploading go through the Xcode account, not the App Store Connect
8	# API key — see release-env.sh for the measurement behind that.
9	#
10	# The build number is the commit count: monotonic, reproducible, and never
11	# stored in the repository — so releasing does not require a version-bump
12	# commit for anything but MARKETING_VERSION.
13	set -euo pipefail
14	
15	# shellcheck source=Scripts/release-env.sh
16	. "$(dirname "$0")/release-env.sh"
17	
18	upload=true
19	require_development_team
20	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
21	  case "$1" in
22	  --no-upload) upload=false ;;
23	  *)
24	    echo "usage: release-ios.sh [--no-upload]" >&2
25	    exit 2
26	    ;;
27	  esac
28	  shift
29	done
30	
31	BUILD_NUMBER="$(git rev-list --count HEAD)"
32	ARCHIVE=Apps/DerivedData/Archives/ReachyMini-iOS.xcarchive
33	
34	set -o pipefail
35	# COMPILATION_CACHE_ENABLE_CACHING=NO: the shipping artifact gets a clean,
36	# uncached compile. The cache went on by default the day before 0.1.1 was
37	# archived, and 0.1.1 is the build that installed from TestFlight with no
38	# Shortcuts actions at all — an archive is rare enough that replayed
39	# compilations buy nothing worth that variable. The metadata check below is
40	# what proves the archive either way, before anything is uploaded.
41	xcodebuild archive \
42	  -workspace Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace -scheme ReachyMini \
43	  -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -configuration Release \
44	  -archivePath "$ARCHIVE" -derivedDataPath Apps/DerivedData \
45	  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$REACHY_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic \
46	  CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION="$BUILD_NUMBER" \
47	  COMPILATION_CACHE_ENABLE_CACHING=NO \
48	  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
49	  -skipPackagePluginValidation -skipMacroValidation \
50	  2>&1 | xcsift
51	
52	# An archive whose Metadata.appintents came out empty ships an app with no
53	# actions in the Shortcuts app, and nothing in the build reddens over it.
54	Scripts/check-appintents-metadata.sh "$ARCHIVE"
55	
56	EXPORT_OPTIONS="$(appstore_export_options "$upload")"
57	
58	xcodebuild -exportArchive \
59	  -archivePath "$ARCHIVE" \
60	  -exportOptionsPlist "$EXPORT_OPTIONS" \
61	  -exportPath Apps/DerivedData/Export/iOS \
62	  -allowProvisioningUpdates \
63	  2>&1 | xcsift
64	
65	if [ "$upload" = true ]; then
66	  echo "Uploaded build $BUILD_NUMBER to App Store Connect. TestFlight shows it after processing (minutes)."
67	else
68	  # The archive was already checked, but the .ipa is what actually ships, and
69	  # -exportArchive re-signs and repacks on the way — so prove the metadata
70	  # survived the export too. Only the --no-upload path leaves an .ipa behind;
71	  # `destination: upload` hands the artifact straight to App Store Connect.
72	  IPA="$(ls Apps/DerivedData/Export/iOS/*.ipa | head -1)"
73	  UNPACKED="$(mktemp -d -t reachy-ipa-check)"
74	  ditto -x -k "$IPA" "$UNPACKED"
75	  Scripts/check-appintents-metadata.sh "$UNPACKED"/Payload/*.app
76	  echo "Exported without uploading:"
77	  ls Apps/DerivedData/Export/iOS/*.ipa
78	fi

Состояние понятно: дерево чистое, последний билд в TestFlight — 143/0.2.3, новый коммит `0629223` даёт 144. Keychain отвечает (не залочен), Apple ID в Xcode на месте.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Номер сборки здесь — это `git rev-list --count HEAD`, а не поле в проекте: версия остаётся 0.2.3, а 144 > 143, чего ASC и требует. Бампить `MARKETING_VERSION` для беты не нужно.
- Обе цели «только TestFlight» = один канал: iOS `release:ios`, macOS `release:macos --channel appstore`. Developer ID (notarize + zip) пропускаем — это артефакт для GitHub-релиза, а не для TestFlight.
- Оба скрипта архивируют с `COMPILATION_CACHE_ENABLE_CACHING=NO` и прогоняют `check-appintents-metadata.sh` до экспорта — именно эта проверка ловит пустой `Metadata.appintents`, из-за которого 0.1.1 уехал в TestFlight без действий Shortcuts, при зелёной сборке.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
